proposal.title: IBM Cloud sensor anomaly detection pipeline (first sketch)
proposal.body: Scope: ingestion, durable buffering, validation, anomaly inference, results storage and operator alerting on IBM Cloud for synthetic sensor events. Assumptions: region not selected and no account access verified. The model is unspecified (labels unknown). None of these components has a native Terraform generator yet, so engineering is required. Local tests use scripted model outputs only.

data.label: Synthetic sensor producer
data.description: Existing synthetic event generator. It emits {deviceId, timestamp (ISO-8601 UTC), metric, value, unit}. It is outside provisioning scope.

data.label: Raw events topic
data.description: Kafka topic 'sensor-raw', keyed by deviceId to keep per-device order. It provides durable buffering with configurable retention, so consumers can replay events.

data.label: Event validator
data.description: Consumer app that checks the schema, device identity, timestamp format and allowed units. It passes valid events through unchanged. Rejected events go to the dead-letter topic with a reason.

data.label: Rejected events topic
data.description: Dead-letter topic 'sensor-rejected' for invalid events, kept for review and replay.

data.label: Anomaly scoring
data.description: Online deployment that scores validated events and returns an anomaly score and flag, with deviceId, timestamp and unit echoed back. The model type is not yet chosen. Locally, a scripted response stands in for it.

data.label: Anomaly results
data.description: Stores one document per scored event (deviceId, timestamp, value, unit, score, flag, model version), with idempotent ids.

data.label: Operator alert
data.description: Sends an alert when an event is flagged as anomalous. The destination (email or Slack, for example) is still to be decided.

data.label: Operator
data.description: Person who receives and handles anomaly alerts.

requirementDrafts.rationale: If identity, time or units are lost or converted, operators could act on the wrong device or misread values.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Preserve device identity, timestamps and units."
requirementDrafts.statement: Every stored result and alert keeps the source deviceId, original timestamp and unit unchanged.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Bad input silently scored would produce false alarms or hide real anomalies.
requirementDrafts.basis: User asked for validation and durable buffering.
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: invalid events go to a dead-letter topic with a rejection reason, are never scored, and can be replayed.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Mocks prove the wiring, not detection quality. Without a time-based evaluation, false-alarm rates are unknown.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation"
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: anomaly model quality is accepted only after evaluation on held-out data from a later time period. Mocked responses count as pipeline tests only.

Do not just recite a checklist or demand that a junior developer repair product internals. Offer a concrete supported correction when possible; otherwise ask one focused question and explain why its answer matters. Help improve this architecture from its current emulation results. Diagnose the first actionable finding. Propose a minimal supported architecture correction only when requirements already justify it; otherwise ask one precise question.
Preserve all required components, existing systems, IDs, established service choices, access boundaries and requirements. Never clear unfinished-work gates, remove workload scope, weaken tests or invent successful validation. A graph proposal cannot repair generator/runtime source or an emulator defect: identify that as product engineering work with a reproducer. Model output is not test evidence. A local emulation pass is not a cloud plan or deployment. After an applied correction, rerun emulation on the new artifact; do not reuse this result. response.message: Good news first: the emulation run came back with no failures. That means our design hangs together. All 8 components are connected, the flow is complete, and nothing in it contradicts our requirements. The status is blocked for a different reason. None of the IBM services we picked (Event Streams, Code Engine, watsonx.ai, Cloudant, Event Notifications) has a supported generator contract yet, and the two existing parts (the sensor producer and the operator) still need a plan for how we connect to them. So nothing could actually run locally. The only supported IBM contract today is private object storage, and switching to it would shrink our pipeline down to storage, which you've ruled out. So I'm leaving the diagram as it is. To close this gap, the product team needs to build native IBM support, starting with an Event Streams topic and dead-letter topic plus a Code Engine validator that keeps deviceId, timestamp and unit unchanged. This exact run can serve as the test case to reproduce it (artifact 3046e8dc…, revision 2). Before that work gets scoped, there's one choice that shapes the model and how we test it: do you have labelled examples of past anomalies, or should we start with an unlabelled scoring approach and accept more false alarms at first?
